decision_titles: Certificate of Appropriateness for 533 Main Street
plain_text:
The City of   Fitchburg 
                                        Massachusetts 
                    Historical Commission 
             718 Main Street, Fitchburg, MA 01420 
                    http://www.ci.fitchburg.ma.us/327/Historical-Commission 
 
Meeting Minutes – September 10, 2026  
1. Call to Order and Attendance 
The meeting was called to order with a quorum present. Attending: Emily Randall, Charles 
Sternaimolo, Keith Chenot - Chair, Don Ostrowski, and Mary Self.  
2. Public Comment 
The Chair opened the meeting for public comments on agenda items. No members of the public 
came forward for general comment. 
3. Approval of Minutes 
The Commission reviewed the minutes of the July 9, 2026, meeting. 
Motion to approve: Don Ostrowski; Seconded – Charles Sternaimolo 
Result: Motion passed unanimously. 
The Commission also reviewed the August 13, 2026, public hearing minutes. 
Motion to approve: Charles Sternaimolo; Seconded – Don Ostrowski 
Result: Motion passed unanimously. 
4. Continued Public Hearing – 533 Main Street 
The Commission continued the public hearing regarding the application for a Certificate of 
Appropriateness for 533 Main Street by Waverly & Sons LLC. Representatives of the 
development team – Jacob Zapata & Alex Dillon from Tocci Group and  
Michael LaFlash from Epsilon Associates - presented revised plans and updates addressing 
issues discussed during previous meetings and the Commission's recent site visit.
The Commission reviewed the proposed exterior colors and masonry restoration. The 
development team recommended retaining the existing upper-floor color scheme using 
professionally matched colors rather than attempting to strip the masonry and recreate an 
uncertain original 1890s appearance. For the first-floor brownstone, testing showed that painting 
the stone produced an artificial appearance. The preferred approach is to preserve and clean the 
exposed natural stone wherever practical. 
The Commission discussed restoring definition to the historic brownstone coursing, particularly 
around the large Main Street arch and along the Main and Fox Street elevations. The 
development team agreed to lightly groove and restrike the joints to better express the individual 
stones. A compatible lime-based mortar will be used for masonry repairs. Replacement masonry 
will be integrated with existing masonry to minimize visible differences. 
The Commission reviewed black and bronze finish samples for the storefront and replacement 
windows. Following discussion, black was selected for the storefront system and replacement 
window frames. Glazing will be clear and non-reflective. The development team explained that 
restoration of approximately fifty-two severely deteriorated existing windows would 
significantly increase both project cost and schedule. The Commission accepted the proposed 
replacement window approach. 
The storefront will retain historically compatible proportions and detail. Lower bulkhead panels 
will have a recessed/picture-frame appearance and remain 18–20 inches high. Proposed entrance 
doors will incorporate an eight-light configuration with substantial lower kick panels. 
5. Entrances, Accessibility, and Exterior Changes 
The Main Street commercial entrance requires an accessible ramp because the interior floor is 
approximately ten inches above sidewalk level. The proposed design includes a ramp along the 
storefront, a large landing, steps on the opposite side, and a black powder-coated aluminum 
railing designed to resemble wrought iron. Entrances will be recessed to prevent doors from 
swinging into the public sidewalk. 
A completed property survey affected the proposed rear egress arrangement. Because access 
through the neighboring rear property is not expected to be available, the rear egress was 
eliminated and the building's egress configuration revised to use Fox Street. 
A new recessed doorway will be created on the Fox Street elevation and coordinated with the 
other entrances. The existing brownstone will be preserved or restored wherever practical. Where 
a historic window opening has been blocked, the material will be removed and the window 
restored. The revised configuration maintains three first-floor residential units while providing 
additional commercial space.
The previous rear opening will be returned to a window. Removed brickwork will be replaced in 
kind with coursing matched to the existing masonry. Historic stone components will be reused 
where practical. 
Because the rear property cannot be used as originally anticipated, an on-site rear dumpster is no 
longer proposed. Trash will instead be managed through regular pickup service. 
6. Roof, Mechanical Systems, and Other Details 
The existing historic chimney will remain, although it is no longer operational. The rooftop 
access penthouse will also remain with its natural copper finish. 
Mechanical equipment will be located toward the center of the roof to minimize visibility from 
the street. Restaurant exhaust and fresh-air systems will penetrate the roof rather than the historic 
exterior façades. 
Required fire-protection equipment will be installed, with historically compatible finishes 
considered where options are available. Residential mailboxes will be located inside the building 
rather than on the exterior. 
7. Certificate of Appropriateness 
Following the presentation and Commission questions, a motion was made and seconded to close 
the public hearing. 
Motion to close the public hearing for the 533 Main Street application: Emily Randall; 
Seconded – Don Ostrowski 
Result: Motion passed. 
The Commission returned to its regular meeting and deliberated on the application. Members 
expressed satisfaction with the revisions and the development team's response to concerns raised 
throughout the review process. 
Motion to grant the Certificate of Appropriateness for 533 Main Street: Emily Randall; 
Seconded – Charles Sternaimolo 
Result: Motion passed 
The Chair will prepare a draft Certificate of Appropriateness. The draft will be circulated to 
Commission members before issuance, and the Building Commissioner will receive the official 
document. 
The development team reported that Historical Commission approval was the remaining 
approval required before obtaining the full building permit. Pauper's Pantry is anticipated to open
in approximately twelve months, although work on residential units may continue beyond that 
point. 
 
 
8. Monument Park Local Historic District 
The Commission reported that informational letters had been mailed to property owners within 
the Monument Park Local Historic District as a periodic reminder regarding their properties' 
inclusion in the district. 
9. Remaining Business and Next Meeting 
Due to the length of the 533 Main Street public hearing and discussion, the Commission agreed 
to postpone the remaining agenda items. 
The next meeting of the Fitchburg Historical Commission is scheduled for Thursday, October 
8, 2026.  
10. Adjournment 
Motion to adjourn: Charles Sternaimolo; Seconded – Mary Self 
Result: Motion passed unanimously. 
The meeting was adjourned.
